subject: Quota uplift and ingress pacing plan for Streamline Labs launch
messages:
From: Maya Rivera <maya@streamlinelabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch day traffic profile + temporary quota request

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We confirmed the feature flag schedule with our product team and expect the public rollout to happen over a 72-hour window starting 2026-09-01 00:00 UTC. Key ask: can Redwood temporarily increase our per-minute token quota and provide a short-term sustained per-second concurrency bump for the first 36 hours?

Attached is a preliminary forecast (launch_traffic_forecast.csv) that shows expected daily token volume and peak ingress per 15-minute window. Conservative peak estimate: 2.4M tokens/hour and ~220 concurrent requests at 99th percentile for a 20-second average completion.

We'd like to finalize a mutual action plan this week so we can get the approval from our platform lead. If you need more granular traffic slices, tell me what format and we'll send it.

Thanks,
Maya Rivera
Head of Integrations, Streamline Labs

Attachments: launch_traffic_forecast.csv (CSV forecast), ops_runbook_v1.pdf (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rivera <maya@streamlinelabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch day traffic profile + temporary quota request

Maya —

Appreciate the file. We can work this but need to align across product, infra, and our capacity ops team. Karthik/Neha — looping you in to confirm what we can support and the gating items.

Immediate asks from our side:
- A 36-hour temporary quota uplift for the account (token limit and concurrency).
- A paced ingress policy to avoid cluster hot spots (we prefer a token-per-second ramp schedule).
- Clear rollback triggers (errors > 5% or latency SLO breaches).

Maya, would you be able to produce a 1-hour per-minute breakdown for the first 36 hours (CSV or sheet) with a per-region split if any traffic is not US-only? That will let us pick a safe concurrency cap.

I attached a short template (ingress-pacing-matrix.xlsx) for the pacing matrix — fill in if helpful. We'll treat this as a temporary raise and put a timebox on it (48–72 hours) with automatic back-to-normal unless mutually extended.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ingress-pacing-matrix.xlsx (template)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch day traffic profile + temporary quota request

Team —

Quick notes from the sales/CS side: Streamline is in their final QA cycle and the release is effectively locked for 2026-09-01. Their legal/procurement are comfortable with a temporary uplift (no contract amendment) if we document the timebox and rollback conditions. They requested pricing guidance for the extra tokens — we'll keep that in a short addendum to the usage invoice.

Product/Infra asks for decisioning:
- Max concurrency we can safely enable for a single account in us-west-2 without impacting other Dedicated customers.
- Whether automatic prefix/KV cache warming is available for their call patterns to reduce cold-start token cost during the first hour.
- A suggested ramp schedule (e.g., 0% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 4 hours) we can present as standard practice.

If we can get a provisional number today, I'll confirm with Streamline and ask them to fill the pacing matrix.

Karthik
Account Lead

[one-line reply note from Maya quoted below]
> Maya Rivera wrote:
> Thanks — will attempt to provide the per-minute slice by EOD.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch day traffic profile + temporary quota request

Folks —

I reviewed the CSV Maya sent. A few operational notes and our ask of Streamline:
1) Please confirm if any calls will include long-generation sequences (>1024 tokens) — those materially affect concurrency.
2) Split by client-region is critical; if traffic is multi-region we recommend edge routing to avoid cross-region latencies.
3) Suggested temporary limits (provisional, subject to infra verification):
   - Token rate cap: 250,000 tokens/minute sustained (approx 15M tokens/hour) — we will throttle above that with 429s.
   - Concurrency cap: 300 concurrent requests (99th pct) for the 36-hour window.
   - Ramp policy: start at 25% for first hour, step to 50% at hour 4, 75% at hour 12, 100% at hour 24.

I've attached a short request PDF (temp_quota_change_request.pdf) that the infra team can use to process the temporary rule. Aditya — can you confirm whether we can set these as a scoped account override in us-west-2 and whether prefix caching can be pre-warmed? Also, can we provision automated telemetry to capture error and latency rates for the rollback triggers?

Neha
Solutions Engineering

Attachments: temp_quota_change_request.pdf (quota change form)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch day traffic profile + temporary quota request

Confirming infra-side clearance: we can implement the scoped override in us-west-2 for the 36-hour window with the caps Neha suggested. Implementation notes:
- Token cap will be enforced via a token-leaky-bucket policy at the account level.
- Concurrency cap will be enforced by a short-lived reservation layer; excess requests will receive 429s with Retry-After headers.
- We can pre-warm KV/prefix caches for their expected top-100 prompts as long as Streamline provides sample prompts by 2026-08-25.
- Telemetry: we'll stream a dedicated trace tag (streamline_launch=DL-8742) and an alert will fire if p95 latency exceeds 2.5s or error rate >5% sustained for 5 minutes.

Operational next steps:
1) Streamline to upload the filled ingress-pacing-matrix.xlsx and per-minute CSV by 2026-08-21 23:59 UTC.
2) Marissa/Karthik to sign off on the final ramp schedule and pricing addendum.
3) Infra to schedule the override for 2026-09-01 00:00 UTC with a hard end time of 2026-09-03 12:00 UTC (36 hours + 12-hour buffer).

I'll open the temp rule ticket once we get the filled matrix and sample prompts. Good to go pending those artifacts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Capacity & Ops, Redwood Inference
